title: Brain Structure — Illustrated Overview
content_html:
Brain Structure — Illustrated Overview

Cerebrum & Cerebral Cortex

The cerebrum comprises the bilateral hemispheres and the multilayered cerebral cortex overlying white-matter tracts. The cortex supports perception, language, planning, working memory, and executive control, with columnar microcircuits enabling parallel distributed processing.

Frontal Lobe

Executive functions (planning, inhibition, decision-making), working memory, voluntary motor control, and language production (Broca’s area). Strong coupling to basal ganglia and cerebellum via fronto-striatal-cerebellar loops.

Parietal Lobe

Multisensory integration, spatial attention, body schema, number and symbol manipulation; dorsal visual stream interfaces with premotor systems for action.

Temporal Lobe

Audition, speech comprehension (Wernicke’s area), semantic memory, object recognition; medial temporal structures (hippocampus, entorhinal cortex) underpin episodic memory.

Occipital Lobe

Visual processing: from edges and orientation (V1) to increasingly complex features in extrastriate cortex.

Limbic System

Emotion–memory circuitry integrating hippocampus (episodic encoding/replay), amygdala (salience and affective tagging), cingulate cortex (conflict monitoring, motivation), fornix/mammillary bodies (declarative memory pathways), and nucleus accumbens (reward-based learning).

Thalamus

Gateway for sensory relays and attention; participates in thalamo-cortical oscillations that scaffold sleep, consciousness, and selective processing.

Hypothalamus

Homeostatic control (temperature, hunger, circadian rhythm), endocrine regulation (pituitary), and motivational states interfacing with limbic signals.

Basal Ganglia

Action selection, habit formation, procedural learning, and reward prediction via dopaminergic signaling (substantia nigra, ventral tegmental input). Direct/indirect pathways regulate facilitation vs suppression of actions.

Cerebellum

Predictive models for movement and cognition; error-driven learning tunes internal timing, coordination, and cognitive sequencing through cortico-cerebellar loops.

Brainstem

Midbrain (reflexes, dopamine), pons (cerebellar relay, sleep), medulla (autonomic functions), with reticular formation modulating arousal and attention.

Large-Scale Networks

  • Default Mode Network (DMN): autobiographical memory, mental time travel, self-referential processing.
  • Salience Network: detects behaviorally relevant stimuli; switches between DMN and executive systems.
  • Central Executive Network: working memory, planning, problem solving.
  • Hippocampal–Cortical Loops: consolidation/replay integrating episodic traces with neocortical models.

Select – Change – Reconstruct (Integration)

Phase Neural Basis Key Structures
Select
(attention & encoding)		 Salience competition, top–down biasing, thalamo-cortical rhythms Thalamus, prefrontal & parietal cortex, amygdala
Change
(plasticity & consolidation)		 Synaptic modification, hippocampal replay, cerebellar error learning Hippocampus, basal ganglia, cerebellum
Reconstruct
(recall & imagination)		 Pattern completion, DMN integration with current goals Hippocampus, medial PFC, temporal cortex
